name: Shlok Agrawal
bio: I’m a mechanical engineering student at Boston University, concentrating in robotics. I’m interested in the space between thoughtful design and working hardware.
about:
My interests span mechanical design, robotics, and manufacturing. I’m drawn to multidisciplinary problems that connect precise engineering with useful, tangible outcomes.

At Boston University’s College of Engineering, I’m concentrating in robotics and developing a practice grounded in curiosity, clear reasoning, and hands-on exploration.

projects.title: Mapping across ground & air.
projects.summary: Combining ground and aerial data to develop a drone-and-rover system for detailed 3D mapping.
projects.problem: Bring together ground and aerial perspectives for detailed 3D mapping within a robotics lab project.
projects.decisions: Applied simultaneous localization and mapping (SLAM) to integrate ground and aerial data. Detailed algorithm choices and design trade-offs will be added with the technical documentation.
projects.development: Developed the drone-and-rover mapping system during a robotics lab internship in Surat. Alongside this work, mentored RC car, boat, and waste-cleaning device builds.
projects.results: Developed a system for detailed 3D mapping. Test datasets, mapping accuracy, and quantitative performance results will be added as supporting material becomes available.

projects.title: Better localization through SLAM.
projects.summary: Research into localization accuracy and efficiency through sensor fusion and SLAM optimization.
projects.problem: Explore how sensor fusion and algorithm optimization can improve simultaneous localization and mapping for robotic navigation.
projects.decisions: Focused the research on sensor fusion and optimization to address localization accuracy and efficiency. Specific algorithm comparisons will be documented alongside the paper.
projects.development: Conducted individual research into applications of SLAM for robotics, UAVs, and autonomous navigation.
projects.results: Produced research on improving localization precision. The paper, experimental methods, and quantitative comparisons will be added to this case study.

projects.title: From CAD to the production floor.
projects.summary: Robot setup, precision fixtures, and the practical work of turning CAD designs into fabricated parts.
projects.problem: Support a high-precision fabrication project while coordinating production across multiple shifts.
projects.decisions: Designed jigs and fixtures for the project’s precision requirements. Geometry, tolerance choices, and manufacturing trade-offs will be added with the supporting drawings.
projects.development: Programmed and set up a Fanuc robot. Converted CAD designs into fabricated parts and coordinated production work across multi-shift teams.
projects.results: Contributed robot programming, fixture design, and fabricated components. Inspection results, tolerances, and production metrics will be added when available.
